subject: MATHEMATICS
purpose: Consumer bindings for the internal-semantics -> learner-copy boundary. This file deliberately holds NO ban-list of its own: the authority is LearnerProduct/policies/math-learner-language-policy.json, which #351 established as the central learner-language policy. What lives here is only the stage-to-falsifier mapping each consumer needs, plus the small set of legacy tokens Core1A already banned before that policy existed, so adopting the policy cannot narrow what Core1A already caught.

consumers.note: Core2A's quality profile declares CORE2A_LEARNER_JARGON_LEAK and no separate identifier code, so an identifier leak is raised under the same declared falsifier rather than inventing an undeclared one.

legacy_core1a_tokens_note: Core1A enforced these before the central policy existed. They are unioned with the policy's forbidden_learner_terms rather than replaced, so nothing Core1A already refused can be lost by adopting the policy. They are intentionally not copied into the policy file: they are Core1A authoring artefacts, not general learner-language rules.
notes: Core2A declared CORE2A_INTERNAL_JARGON_LEAK in its quality profile and the central policy declared the vocabulary, but until this phase no engine scanned learner text against either. LearnerRealization/engine/learner_copy.py is that engine, and each consumer keeps its own falsifier prefix so no existing vocabulary is replaced.
run_learner_product.py binds MATH-LEARNER-LANGUAGE-v1 by policy id only (a binding-drift check). This registry plus learner_copy.py is what makes the bound policy enforceable against actual text.
